conversation: Fix StepKit so the project/take-it-away workflow can successfully recover and continue after interrupted runs. Context from investigation: the latest take-it-away run `.stepkit/runs/take-it-away-20260804-133215-41575ba3` was retried, but the workflow still failed. Key problems to implement, with behavioral-red TDD and protection of all pre-existing work: (1) Fix take-it-away/create-flows story durability: the story loop currently removes a selected story from `storyQueue` before the story is reviewed/completed, so an interruption leaves it absent from both `storyQueue` and `completedStories`. Add durable active/current story tracking or defer removal until review passes, with regression coverage. (2) Fix core retry for dangling active steps: if the last event is `step.started` with no terminal event because the runner died, `stepkit retry` currently says there is no latest unresolved failure. Retry should detect this stale active step and safely retry it or append/interpret an interrupted failure marker. Add tests. (3) Fix retry for workflow-level failures without `stepId`: when a step returns `fail(...)`, runtime can emit only `workflow.failed`, and retry later fails with `Failed step event has no step id.` Add step source metadata or emit a step-scoped failure so retry can target the failed step. Add tests. (4) Fix reviewer baseline in project-take-it-away: the workflow or agent commits story changes during a run, and reviewers appear to inspect only uncommitted diffs, causing false review failures claiming committed files are missing. Store/use a story start commit and make review inspect `git diff <storyStartCommit>..HEAD` plus uncommitted diff, or otherwise ensure reviewers see the entire story slice. Add regression coverage if practical. (5) Fix event ID uniqueness: `packages/core/src/runtime/events/create-run-event.ts` still uses a process-local counter, and duplicate event ids appeared after retry. Use UUID/ULID or seed from persisted events; event ordering must remain JSONL/replay order. Add tests. (6) Avoid blindly retrying the existing failed run until these fixes are in place; after fixes, either start a fresh run or provide a safe recovery path. Preserve provider-level CLI `--resume` repair behavior; StepKit workflow `--resume` UX should remain removed. Run focused validations for each slice and report exactly what changed.
